title: Bounty Hunting - The Ghoul Lore & Dialogue
blurb: Who The Ghoul is in Fallout 76, where he turns up in every region, what he lets slip about himself, his Billie codename, and every line he says, laid out as the conversation menus you see in game.

sections.title: Who Is The Ghoul?
sections.html:
The Ghoul runs bounty hunting in Burning Springs. He works out of The Last Resort, the saloon in Highway Town, and hands out Grunt Hunts and Head Hunts from a stack of contracts.

He is Cooper Howard from the Fallout TV series, voiced by Walton Goggins, and arrived with the Burning Springs update (per Bethesda). In the game files he is only ever "The Ghoul", and his voice type is labelled "Bounty Hunter".

What he lets slip

  • He isn't from Ohio, and he isn't saying where he's from: "Where I'm from is one of those things that's not your concern."
  • He's here for a reason: "Let's just say I followed somebody out here. Somebody I'd very much like to meet."
  • He's been looking into the Vaults. He tells a fresh Vault 76 dweller he "already interrogated the last one of you to come out of that hole. Sounds like there's nothing down there for me."
  • He doesn't care what a target did, "so long as the caps from the bounty end up in my pocket to pay for the chems in my lungs." He stays at The Last Resort because "the barkeep here's got the vials I like".
  • On the Rust King: "Not the first would-be king I've seen in the Wasteland. Doubt he'll be the last... All I know is kings fall, and all crowns rust."
  • His one rule for bounty hunters: "We don't do 'dead or alive'. Just dead."

In the TV show he's searching for his family, which fits "followed somebody out here". Nothing in the Fallout 76 files names who he's following, though.

sections.title: Where to Find Him
sections.html:
His home is The Last Resort, the saloon in Highway Town, Burning Springs. He stands against the back wall.

Before you've been to Burning Springs, he can also turn up in every region of Appalachia, standing over a target he's just killed. He tells you about Burning Springs ("burnt clean away after the war"), points you to the bridge by Point Pleasant, and says to find him at The Last Resort.

sections.title: Billie Is The Ghoul
sections.html:
Billie and The Ghoul are the same person. Bethesda used the name Billie as a codename, so data miners wouldn't spot The Ghoul in the files before he was revealed.

The codename version is still in the files. It has its own set of lines ("Give me a premium target", the 5,000-cap fee, "Wasteland's full of confident dead guys") and is set up in the exact same spot in The Last Resort. The two versions share one switch, so only one is ever standing there, and in game it's The Ghoul.

The codename lines are at the bottom of this page.

sections.title: Buying a Wanted Poster
sections.html:
Burning Springs Wanted Posters are bought from him through dialogue, not a shop menu:

  1. First time: "Got anything better than these grunts?" → "Tell me about these “juicy” targets." → "Give me a premium target." → "[5,000 Caps] All right, here's your caps."
  2. After that: "Give me a premium target." → "[5,000 Caps] All right, here's your caps."

You need 5,000 caps on you. If you already have a Burning Springs Wanted Poster: "No can do, hoss. One per customer."

docs.name: Bounty Draft - Lemon Boys
docs.text:
"Bounty Draft"

~ WANTED ~
For Mass Murder, Highway Robbery, Damage of town Property, and Racketeering Charges.

~ DEAD ONLY ~
THE LEMON BOY GANG

Gang Members: Robyn the Brute, Darwin the Devil and Archie the Kid.
Reward: 2,000 caps each.
Last Seen: Camping South Of The Old Lake, near the collapsed tunnel.

- - - - - -
These criminals are armed and dangerous. Extreme caution is advised.

Warning: I won't be putting this up to claim, the person who has requested the bounty does not have the caps to pay the reward

groups.title: Talking to The Ghoul at The Last Resort

items.prompt: I don't know what you're talking about.
I'm sorry, what?
What's it to you?
lines: What it is, is business. Business that just might be of interest to someone of your...disposition.

items.prompt: Is that a threat?
lines: Now, let's put that hostility on ice for a spell, hotshot. Hands away from the iron.
If I meant you harm, you'd already know it. I've got a little proposition, if you'll shut up and listen.
I happen to run a little service for the folks of this...charming locale.
See, they ain't got anything you might call law around here. Suits me fine, mind you, but that leaves a lot of bad blood unaddressed.
Generous soul that I am, I match demands for vengeance with bloody-handed individuals like yourself who are eager to deal it out.

items.prompt: Are you talking about assassins?
lines: That's a bit high-falutin' for folks 'round these parts. Call it what it is: bounty huntin'.
Somebody needs somebody else dead and ain't got the stones to handle it themselves, I make the arrangements. For a fee, of course.
conds: Only until: asked assassins

items.prompt: All right, then. Tell me more about bounty hunting.
lines: I had you pegged from the start.
Simple enough arrangement. I collect a fee from the afflicted, and farm out the killin' to motivated individuals such as yourself.
You run down the target in whatever shithole they're hidin' out in and put 'em in the ground, whatever means necessary.
Have fun with it! I know I do.
conds: Only after: asked assassins

items.prompt: Who the hell are you?
lines: Not that kind of rodeo, partner. I don't care who you are and I sure as hell ain't here to share my life story, even if you'd believe me.
You want to talk business, we can. Otherwise, move along. You're classin' up the joint.

items.prompt: I've got some questions about this place, first.
Okay, deal me in. I'll take a bounty.
lines: That's the killer instinct I was looking for! Got a big stack of open contracts right there. Help yourself; more there than I could ever bother with.
Unless you're looking for something juicier. Well, that's a whole different ballgame.

items.prompt: What's in it for me?
lines: Keep what you kill, cowboy. To the victor goes the spoils, as they say.
If someone's bad enough the poor saps here put up money to kill them, odds are they've got something worth taking.
Of course, well, you might just do it for the thrill of it. Or am I mistaken?

items.prompt: I'd like to know more about the lay of the land, first.
I'm not a murderer.
lines: Is that right, hoss? Your path here bathed in blood, and you innocent as the day your momma spat you out?
Well, if it helps you sleep at night, every name I hand out's somebody that has it comin'. Might as well collect 'fore someone else does.

items.prompt: I guess I'm off, then.
lines: Remember: we don't do "dead or alive". Just dead.

items.prompt: That easy? What's the catch?
lines: That easy. Those contracts aren't worth my very valuable time, so I'm happy for you or anyone else to take 'em off my hands.
Unless you're looking for something more exciting. That's a beast of a different color.
conds: Only until: asked catch

items.prompt: You're getting paid. Why am I doing all the work for scraps?
lines: Well, I think you mean you're getting to do the best part, while I sit in this pisshole.
I keep my ear to the ground, you keep your iron in your hand. We'll get along just fine.
A reputation as a killer of killers goes a long way in these parts, if the excitement and looting ain't enough for you.

items.prompt: Why not collect the bounties yourself, if you're already being paid?
lines: Oh, I keep my hand in, from time to time, if the job's interesting enough. Most ain't.
Let's just say the barkeep here's got the vials I like, and I ain't inclined to stray unless properly compelled. Besides...
There's always more folk need killin' than I can be bothered with, anyway.
And here you are.

items.prompt: Sounds like I should just deal with the clients themselves and keep the money.
lines: Assuming you know where to begin, then you'd be competition, wouldn't you?
Lotta folks made that mistake over the years. I'm still here.
They ain't.

items.prompt: What's this about "something more exciting?"
I'm looking for another bounty.
lines: Hah! Knew you'd get the taste for it. Now you're back for more, huh?
No need to get me involved; you know the drill. Peel one off the stack and get to it.
Good huntin'.

items.prompt: Got anything better than these grunts?
conds: Only until: you've heard about head hunts

items.prompt: Give me a premium target.
lines: Hmm...
conds: Only after: you've heard about head hunts

items.prompt: I'd like to know more about the area, if you don't mind.
Actually, never mind.
lines: Last time somebody wasted my time like you, I shot 'em. Keep it up and maybe next bounty's on you.
I can do that. There's just the small matter of my compensation.
conds: Only if you don't have a Wanted Poster

lines: No can do, hoss. One per customer. Gotta finish what's on your plate before you come back for seconds.
conds: Only if you already have a Wanted Poster

items.prompt: [5,000 Caps] All right, here's your caps.
lines: Pleasure doing business with you.
Here's the bounty notice. Take this and post it on the board outside. Let everyone know the hunt is on.
Good huntin'.
conds: Needs 5,000 caps

items.prompt: You want a bribe?
lines: Well, not a bribe entirely. Think of it as greasing the wheels of commerce.
conds: Only until: asked about bribe

items.prompt: What's it going to cost me?
lines: Probably more caps than you're comfortable payin', but... I'm a man of principle, you see.
Principles cost a lot in the Wasteland. Often more than just money. Consider this a bargain.
conds: Only until: asked about bribe

items.prompt: Are you kidding me? You've already made money on this.
lines: Someone once said it was easier to imagine the end of the world than the end of capitalism. Well, they was right.
Now, you want to jump the line...that costs. Your call.

items.prompt: Forget it. I'll come back later.
lines: Just as well. Ain't no half measures in this business.
For the likes of you, anyway. Me, well, I'm here for other libations.
conds: If you are not a ghoul

lines: That ain't a problem for you or me, though, is it?
conds: If you are a ghoul

items.prompt: What are you doing in Ohio? Besides running bounty hunters, I mean.
lines: Maybe I'm just waiting for the right bounty to fall into my lap. Maybe it's none of your business.
Let's just say I followed somebody out here. Somebody I'd very much like to meet. Until we have a face-to-face, well...
A man needs a hobby.

items.prompt: What do you know about the Rust King?
lines: Some overgrown green bastard with delusions of grandeur?
Not the first would-be king I've seen in the Wasteland. Doubt he'll be the last.
He doesn't interfere with my business, I've got no reason to get involved with his.
All I know is kings fall, and all crowns rust.
conds: Only after you have completed Welcoming Committee

items.prompt: I wanted to know about something else.
lines: Of course you do.

items.prompt: What can you tell me about the area?
lines: Ohio? Didn't think much of it before the bombs dropped, and it hasn't improved since.
Never expected a desert out this way, though. Somebody really fucked it up.

items.prompt: Tell me about Highway Town.
lines: This dump is the only livable place for miles and miles. They've got drinkable water here.
Well, drinkable enough. Everything else in the region is pure poison, never mind the radiation.

items.prompt: You don't sound like a local.
lines: Figured that out all by yourself, did you? No, I am not.
Small mercies, huh? Not that one place is much better than another in the Wasteland.
Where I'm from is one of those things that's not your concern.

items.prompt: Let's talk about something else.
lines: Yeah, I'm bored already.

items.prompt: Tell me about these "juicy" targets.
lines: These are the worst of the worst. Most hunters that go after these targets wind up dead. And that just makes the bounty larger.
Thing is, it's bad for business if I keep sending bounty hunters to their death. People start to think I can't get things done.
So, things work a little differently for these. First off, you post the notice for one of these fellas, it's open season.
Any hunter that wants to can get in on the action, and you'll likely be grateful for the help.
Second, I only allow one of these bounties to be open at once. Somebody else has one posted, you're just gonna have to wait until they're taken out.
Hell, join in if you want!
Most importantly, these are the ones I like to handle myself. If you want one, I need compensation.
conds: Only until: you've heard about head hunts

items.prompt: Give me a premium target.
lines: Well, all right! Full of confidence, eh, cowboy?
Wasteland's full of confident dead guys. Let's see if you've got the stuff to back it up. There's just this little matter of my fee, mind you.
conds: Only after: you've heard about head hunts

items.prompt: I'll stick to regular targets for now.
lines: Suit yourself. You know where to find me.

groups.title: Meeting The Ghoul out in Appalachia

items.prompt: What? Who are you?
lines: Oh, just a workin' man passin' through.
This fella here had a price on his head, and thought he'd run far enough.
He hadn't.

items.prompt: Can I ask you some questions?
lines: Normally, I'd tell you to go to hell, if not shoot you and take anything valuable.
Seein' as this one here just made me a pile of caps and you're still wet behind the ears, I'm feelin' generous.

items.prompt: Wait...there's people alive out here?
lines: A lot more than you might expect, Vaultie, depending on your definition of "people". Best get comfortable with the idea.
There's a lot of folks out there might take advantage of your wide-eyed innocence. Present company included.

items.prompt: Where'd you come from?
lines: Slow down there, cowboy. Buy a fella dinner first. Let's just say I'm currently residing in Burning Springs, across the river in what used to be Ohio.

items.prompt: You killed this person?
lines: He was dead the moment they put a bounty on his sorry ass. This just happens to be where we concluded our business.

items.prompt: What happened to your face?
lines: Hah.
Guess they don't have manners in that Vault of yours.
I'll give you a pass on that this one time, seein' as you just stepped foot into the Wasteland a minute ago.
Same thing that'll happen to your face you stay out here long enough. Ain't the only one, neither. Best get used to the sight.

items.prompt: Can you tell me anything about this area?
lines: This brain ain't for pickin'. Plenty of locals around here who'll talk your ear off, I'm sure.

items.prompt: I think that's enough talk.
lines: Couldn't agree more.
If you get out to Burning Springs, see me at the Last Resort saloon. Might be there's work for you.

loose.quest: Meeting The Ghoul out in Appalachia

lines: Got no time nor inclination for chit-chat.
Find me at the Last Resort in Highway Town if you're lookin' to do business.
conds: Once he has already pointed you to Burning Springs
Once he has already pointed you to Burning Springs

lines: Well, look at you. Fresh from the can and not a speck of dirt on you. Best watch your step around here.
Figured you Vaulties weren't done cooking yet. Guess I was wrong.
Already interrogated the last one of you to come out of that hole. Sounds like there's nothing down there for me, though.
Saves me the trouble of breakin' in.

Before he has pointed you to Burning Springs

loose.quest: Talking to The Ghoul at The Last Resort

lines: Well, now, welcome back, killer.
Just here to wet your whistle, or you lookin' to play for blood?
Not lookin' for friends. Talk business or get lost.
Still alive? Wouldn't've put money on it.
You waiting for something? You've got the bounty. Get on out there, killer.

lines: You again. Didn't think you'd make it this far. Guess you got your hands very dirty indeed.
conds: Only if you have never completed Bounty Hunting: Grunt Hunt

loose.quest: Talking to The Ghoul at The Last Resort

lines: Unless you've got business, keep on walkin'.
Hmm.
Those tin cans ain't all they're cracked up to be, y'know.
conds: If you own power armour

lines: Hnh.
Help yourself to a bounty. There's always more.
conds: Only after you have completed Bounty Hunting: Grunt Hunt

lines: Pile never seems to get smaller. Grab a bounty if you feel like rollin' the dice.
conds: Only after you have completed Bounty Hunting: Grunt Hunt

lines: More where those came from. Help yourself.
conds: Only after you have completed Bounty Hunting: Grunt Hunt

loose.label: Other lines
loose.quest: Meeting The Ghoul out in Appalachia

lines: Keep those hands where I can see 'em, stranger. This one's mine, and I'd prefer my killin' to be for-profit today.
Might want to get your feet under you first. Folks out that way tend to shoot first and forget about questions.
Do what you want, 'cause I ain't your daddy.
You might even survive the experience. Plenty of work out there, if you don't mind killing.
Probably best you worry about yourself for now. This kind of work isn't for lost little lambs like you.
Of course, if that changes - or if you just have a death wish - come look me up sometime.
If you're interested, find me there. I got a feelin' you might be cut out for this sort of thing.

loose.label: Other lines
loose.quest: Talking to The Ghoul at The Last Resort

lines: No need to be shy about it. Locals sure ain't. Or maybe you're just the silent, violent type.
If you're looking for the tourism office, this ain't it.
Ah, what the hell, I'm in a good mood... Best not change that.
The sort of person I'm sending you after is a killer, to be sure, but small potatoes.
Now, if you're hungry for a full meal... I've got contracts out on real sons of bitches.
The kind that put the fear in entire towns and leave a trail of dead bounty hunters in their wake. And I'm not just referring to myself.
I'm talking twelve course dinner. Real juicy targets. I don't give those out to just anyone.
